framework: Serious Injury & Fatality (SIF) Precursor Identification Framework
authoritative_sources: Campbell Institute / National Safety Council: SIF Prevention
Construction Safety Research Alliance (CSRA): High-Energy Control Assessment Project (HECAT)
Dekra / BST: Serious Injury and Fatality Prevention
sif_definition: A high-severity workplace event that resulted in a fatal or life-altering, permanent disabling injury, OR a high-potential precursor event where high energy was present in the absence of an effective, direct control barrier, credibly leading to a fatal or life-altering outcome had the circumstances slightly varied.

required_conditions: Condition 1: High Energy Present or Released (CSRA Energy Wheel definition)
Condition 2: Line of Fire or Direct Exposure of Human Target
Condition 3: Compromised, Missing, or Ineffective Critical Direct Barrier

energy_thresholds.GRAVITATIONAL: Fall from height >= 1.8m (6ft), dropped object with impact energy >= 40 Joules (~2kg dropped from 2m or heavy rigging/pipe)
energy_thresholds.PRESSURE: Hydraulic or pneumatic pressure >= 100 psi (0.7 MPa) or pressurized system volume capable of rapid catastrophic release
energy_thresholds.THERMAL: Open flame, temperature > 60°C liquid contact or > 200°C surface contact capable of 2nd/3rd degree burns, cryogenic release
energy_thresholds.ELECTRICAL: Alternating current voltage >= 50V AC or direct current >= 100V DC capable of ventricular fibrillation or arc flash
energy_thresholds.KINETIC: Heavy vehicle in motion, high-speed rotating equipment, tensioned mooring line / winch under load, parted line snapback zone
energy_thresholds.CHEMICAL: Toxic gas release (H2S >= 10 ppm, CO >= 35 ppm), flammable hydrocarbon vapor cloud (LEL >= 10%), strong acids/caustics

precursor_vs_non_precursor.sif_precursor: An observable unsafe act, unsafe condition, near-miss, or minor event that contains both high energy and compromised barrier elements, requiring only minor situational variation to cause a fatality or permanent disability.
precursor_vs_non_precursor.non_sif_event: Low-energy physical event (e.g. minor slip/trip on flat deck, pinch point without high force, small hand tool abrasion) or an event where reliable engineered barriers remained fully intact and successfully arrested the energy.

label_taxonomy.EXPLICIT: Event narrative or source document explicitly uses definitive regulatory classification (e.g. 'fatality', 'high potential', 'HiPo', 'serious injury potential').
label_taxonomy.DERIVED: Objective presence of high energy + compromised barrier + worker in line-of-fire verified from narrative text.
label_taxonomy.WEAKLY_DERIVED: Plausible exposure but missing either exact worker proximity or exact barrier state.
label_taxonomy.UNKNOWN: Insufficient information in narrative to determine whether high energy was uncontrolled or whether barriers were active.
